subject: Curelytics security follow-up — pen test access & vuln SLA discussion
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Danielle Park <dpark@curelytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-04-12T16:12:00-04:00
Subject: Curelytics security follow-up — pen test access & vuln SLA discussion

Hi Danielle — thanks again for the demo earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment from the security side: 

1) SOC 2 / compliance posture
- You mentioned SOC 2 is currently in flight (Type II expected Q3). Could you confirm the in-scope systems and whether Redwood needs to be included as a subservice?

2) Vendor questionnaire & evidence
- Please send over the vendor security questionnaire. I can route to our security team (Marissa) for responses and attach supporting artifacts (DPA, attestation summary, architecture diagram).

3) Pen test report access + vuln management
- Per your ask: we can provide a pen-test summary immediately and arrange controlled access to the full report. Typical handback flow is: summary (public) -> gated full report (requires MSA/NDA/secure link) -> remediation notes (if applicable).

4) Remediation SLA & scanning cadence (proposal)
- Recommended default SLAs: Critical: 14 calendar days; High: 30 days; Medium: 90 days.
- Scanning cadence: weekly external unauthenticated scans, monthly authenticated scans for infra changes, quarterly full internal/external pen tests.

Next steps I propose:
- Danielle: drop the vendor questionnaire or paste the link (we’ll start answers)
- Redwoods (Marissa + Sean): provide pen-test summary + SOC2 progress doc within 48 hours; scope gated report delivery on NDA
- I'll schedule a 30-min follow-up call next week to walk the questionnaire and clarify SLAs

Attaching the pen-test summary and SOC2 overview for initial review (attached).

Best,
Aditya
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com
+1 415-555-0198

Attachments: redwood-penreport-summary-2026.pdf, SOC2-progress-overview-2027.pdf
From: Danielle Park <dpark@curelytics.com>

Cc: Security Ops <security@curelytics.com>, Jacob Lee <jlee@curelytics.com>
Date: 2027-04-12T18:03:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Curelytics security follow-up — pen test access & vuln SLA discussion

Thanks Aditya — useful summary. A few items from our side: 

- SOC 2: we are tracking vendor coverage for PII handling services. Please confirm whether Redwood will be willing to be listed as a subservice (we require documentation showing in-scope controls).

- Vendor questionnaire: attaching our standard security questionnaire (DOCX) and a short intake checklist. Please have your security team fill Qs 1-25; the rest are optional depending on answers.

- Pen test: we need (a) a non-sensitive public summary to share with our procurement team and (b) access to the full report under an NDA. Also need to understand your vulnerability disclosure policy and remediation SLAs — the procurement must sign off on timelines.

- Scanning cadence: please provide the exact scans you run and whether authenticated scans include app creds or are network-only.

I’ll loop in Jacob (security engineer) for technical review. We’d like the initial artifacts by EOD Thursday if possible so procurement can review ahead of next Friday's vendor committee.

Regards,
Danielle Park
Head of Procurement | Curelytics
dpark@curelytics.com

Attachment: Curelytics-Vendor-Security-Questionnaire.docx
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-04-13T09:02:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Curelytics security follow-up — pen test access & vuln SLA discussion

Looping in with concrete answers and a suggested artifact package for Curelytics. Draft below for Aditya to send (I’ll review before send):

- SOC 2: Redwood completed SOC 2 Type I in 2025; Type II testing is in progress with expected completion August 2027. In our vendor pack we provide: SOC 2 summary letter, scope matrix (services in scope), and control-owner slides. We can be listed as a subservice — recommend a short statement clarifying which SaaS components are covered.

- Pen test: we can share three artifacts today: (1) redwood-penreport-summary-2026.pdf (non-sensitive exec summary), (2) SOC2-progress-overview-2027.pdf, (3) Redwood-DPA-v2-2027.pdf. Full pen-test report is shared via secure link after a mutual NDA. Our standard vulnerability SLA is as follows: Critical — 14 days, High — 30 days, Medium — 90 days. Coordinated disclosure window: 30 days from initial report unless the customer requests otherwise.

- Scanning cadence: weekly external unauthenticated scans (Rapid7), monthly authenticated scans (internal creds for app layer), and quarterly full scope pen tests by third-party vendor. We also run continuous dependency scanning on CI with SCA and auto-alerts to SECOPS.

- Access control for full reports: we require an executed mutual NDA and an access request form (company legal name, security contacts). We also prefer that clients do not redistribute the full report beyond the security and procurement reviewers.

I’ll attach the three artifacts to the email for send. Let me know if we should soften any SLA language for procurement.

-Marissa
Sr. Security Program Manager | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com

Attachments: redwood-penreport-summary-2026.pdf, SOC2-progress-overview-2027.pdf, Redwood-DPA-v2-2027.pdf
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Danielle Park <dpark@curelytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-04-13T11:24:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Curelytics security follow-up — pen test access & vuln SLA discussion

Danielle — thanks. Per Marissa’s note I’ve attached the three artifacts for your procurement packet and pasted our proposed answers inline below for the first 10 questionnaire items (we’ll upload full doc once Marissa completes the remaining fields).

Quick answers (excerpts):
- Q1: SOC 2 status — Type I complete (2025); Type II in progress, expected August 2027. Full attestation available post-audit.
- Q4: Data protection/HIPAA — Redwood offers a HIPAA-compliant deployment option; we sign BAAs for covered engagements.
- Q7: GDPR — We have a current DPA and data processing addendum; processing locations and subprocessors are documented in the DPA (attached).
- Q12: Pen-test access — Exec summary attached. Full handback after mutual NDA; request form required.

Vulnerability management & SLA (official):
- Critical: 14 calendar days from confirmed report
- High: 30 calendar days
- Medium: 90 calendar days
- Scanning cadence: weekly external unauthenticated scans; monthly authenticated scans; quarterly third-party pen tests; CI SCA continuous scanning.
- Coordinated disclosure: 30 days (we can adjust per contract)

I’ve also created a secure share link for the gated full report request: https://redwood-secure.s3.amazonaws.com/share/rdw-penreport-2026 (requires link + NDA). If you confirm the signatory for the NDA, I’ll route our legal team to send the mutual NDA (DocuSign) and we can grant access once executed.

Would you be available for a 30-minute call Thursday 4/15 at 10am ET to walk the questionnaire and confirm required artifacts for procurement?

Best,
Aditya

Attachments: redwood-penreport-summary-2026.pdf, SOC2-progress-overview-2027.pdf, Redwood-DPA-v2-2027.pdf
From: Jacob Lee <jlee@curelytics.com>

Cc: Security Ops <security@curelytics.com>
Date: 2027-04-14T10:03:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Curelytics security follow-up — pen test access & vuln SLA discussion

Aditya, Danielle — received the artifacts, thanks. A couple quick confirms from security engineering: 

- The summary and DPA look fine for procurement triage. Please proceed with the NDA and secure link for full report access.
- Our team confirms the proposed SLAs are acceptable as baseline; procurement will include them in the contract with the option to tighten timelines for critical findings.
- For scans: when you say "authenticated scans (internal creds)" — please confirm whether those are performed using ephemeral test accounts or live service accounts. We prefer ephemeral test creds scoped to read-only test environments.

If you can get the NDA over today, I’ll review and route to legal. Also — we’ll accept the 4/15 10am ET call; Danielle will send the invite.

Thanks,
Jacob Lee
Security Engineer | Curelytics
